questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was specifically looking for an exchange opportunity in Spain to improve my Spanish. For me i chose Bilbao because i find the Basque history and culture very interesting, but i also liked the fact that it is less visited than Barcelona or Madrid. I also really liked the fact that it was a smaller city close to nature allowing for hiking. Besides that i had heard a lot about the gastronomical scene in the basque country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think Bilbao as a city is very nice and you definitely get to feel the very special atmosphere and culture in the Basque Country. I really liked the basque people i met on the way, and they were very welcoming towards me and i had some spots around the city where i could feel like a local/regular. On the other hand the study environment is in my opinion not the best. There are not a lot of events or student organizations within the University of the Basque Country. This makes it harder to meet local students, and compared to University of Copenhagen, it would've been nice with friday bars on campus, different events and talks either for the social aspects or as a supplement to the studies. At least for me the only negative part of my experience is that you as a student are left with events coordinated by ESN or Happy Erasmus, so you only really meet other Erasmus students.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think information in regards to UPV (University of the Basque Country) was a bit sparse, but with a buddy student this helped a lot. Although this was only the first few days. I was also lucky enough to have a landlord that was able to help me with finding information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of assistance from Maitane the international student coordinator at UPV, she has been a great help and done a really good job.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult finding housing, but idealista and erasmus whatsapp group helped a lot. Although a lot of hounsing ads seems like a scam. If i were to do it again, i would definitely apply for college/dorms, as the student housing seems really nice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus seems like the most common thing with not a lot of on campus housing. Generally living in Bilbao (Casco Viejo, Abando, Indauxtu, San Francisco, Urribarri, Moyua, San Mamés, Deustu or Santutxu) is nice. And it's easy to get to the different campuses from the city center either by bicycle, metro or bus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not a lot of information in English and i had some difficulties finding schedules for the courses. I think it was generally lack of information.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered for course from back home, but was later able to switch some of the courses, this was really nice as some of my courses were overlapping and with courses not fit for my bachelor.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of help from Maitane the international student coordinator in regards to registering and finding courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was registered for all the classes i wanted and even ended up switching you classes i would much rather have, so this was fairly easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that there are no overlaps and that you consider whether a course is in Spanish (great opportunity to learn the language) or English as well as the criteria to pass the course. But you will be able to change courses in the beginning of the semester. In general just get a few more courses approved from back home and then you will be able to switch out classes that are not what you ecxpected them to be.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Academically it was fairly easy, not the most difficult courses i have had. It generally varied a lot i had a difficult course from the engineering of information, I'm an economics student. But besides that i found the level to be lower than at University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is very different, it's mainly lectures but with emphasis on participation. I found it to be more similar to that of danish high schools than of lectures and then lab/instructor classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Data Mining (Mineria de Datos)
- International Economics
- Regional Economics
- Labour Economics (Economía Laboral)
- Game Theory (Teoría de Juegos)
- Ecodesign and Circular Economy
- Economics of Information

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommen all of the courses i took, besides ecodesign and circular economy. The course i took were fairly easy to participate in for exchange students. I did not like the attitude of the lecturer/professor in ecodesign and circular economy though. The classes was also friday from 16-21 and saturdays.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend to visit the coast of Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa, Vitoria and San Sebastian. It is also really nice visiting Cantabria and Asturias. Some towns outside of Bilbao would be Lekeitoa, El Antxobe, Gernika and Bermeo/Mundaka in the Bizkaia region. Santoña in Cantabria is also really nice. I also like San Francisco and Bilbao la Vieja. Visit the cafe Bihotz, the wine bar Taska Beltz, the pizzeria Demaio and the restaurant Kimtxu. And don't forget to try a menu del dia at midday.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it a bit hard, with different times for eating out and with the stores being closed between 14 and 17. It is also difficult if you don't speak any spanish. But i managed to speak to some locals by being a regular at a few bars and cafes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is very difficult because a lot of students being uncomfortable speaking English or non-English speakers, they also tend to be younger than scandinavian students. But if you speak some spanish or have the courage to do courses in spanish it is definitely easier to meet local students as you will most of the time be the only or one few exchange students in the class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: As i only speak some spanish it was difficult that a big part of the population speaks only Spanish or Spanish and Basque, but it is also a great opportunity for improving spanish proficiency.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pride in the Basque heritage was really interesting, people were very nice and really wanted to show why Bilbao and the Basque Country is such a great place. I liked the pintxos, kalimotxo, the food in general and the vibrant city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Really try to learn spanish
- Visit the different regions, cities and nature of the Basque Country instead of spending all weekends in all of the other cities in spain.
- Don't get to caught up in the Happy Erasmus parties, but it is a great way to find likeminded exchange students

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress to much about school, if you attend classes and do all assignments you're gonna be fine.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning about the culture of the basque country and having the experience of living outside of Denmark. I also met a lot of great people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting to know local people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
